purpose: This medicine is used to treat a condition called Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency, which is an inherited disease that can damage your lungs over time. It helps slow down lung damage in adults who already show signs of lung disease from this condition. Think of it as replacing a natural protein your body is not making enough of on its own.
how_it_works: Normally, your body makes a protein called Alpha-1 Antitrypsin that protects your lungs from being broken down by harmful enzymes. If your body does not make enough of this protein, those enzymes can slowly destroy lung tissue. This medication gives your body the missing protein through an IV infusion, helping to shield your lungs from that damage.
common_side_effects: Some people may experience headache, dizziness, mild fever, chills, or feeling flushed during or after the infusion. You might also notice some fatigue, nausea, or mild injection site reactions. These side effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have ever had a severe allergic reaction to any blood products, since this medicine is made from human plasma. There is a very small risk of viral infection since it comes from donated blood, though the product is carefully screened and treated. If you notice signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, difficulty breathing, or chest tightness during your infusion, let your healthcare provider know right away.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 60 mg per kilogram of your body weight, given once a week through an IV infusion. Your nurse or healthcare provider will give this to you, usually in a clinic or infusion center. Each infusion typically takes about 15 to 30 minutes depending on the brand used.
